full_name: Stochastic Block Mirror Descent for Nonsmooth Convex Stochastic Optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020 (Theorem 4.12)

problem.description: Stochastic convex optimization with block-decomposable feasible set

variable_space.math: X = X_1 \times X_2 \times \cdots \times X_b \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n, \text{ each } X_i \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n_i} \text{ closed convex, } \sum_{i=1}^{b} n_i = n

assumptions.name: Block distance generating functions
assumptions.math: v_i : X_i \to \mathbb{R} \text{ is continuously differentiable and 1-strongly convex w.r.t. } \|\cdot\|_i; \; V_i(z, x) = v_i(x) - [v_i(z) + \langle \nabla v_i(z), x - z \rangle], \; \forall x, z \in X_i

initialization.math: x_1 \in X, \; s_1 = 0, \; u_i = 1 \text{ for } i = 1, \ldots, b

steps.name: Sample block index
steps.math: \text{Generate } i_k \text{ with } \operatorname{Prob}\{i_k = i\} = p_i, \; i = 1, \ldots, b

steps.name: Incremental averaging update
steps.math: s_{k+1}^{(i)} = \begin{cases} s_k^{(i)} + x_k^{(i)} \sum_{j=u_i}^{k} \theta_j, & i = i_k, \\ s_k^{(i)}, & i \ne i_k \end{cases}, \quad \text{then set } u_{i_k} = k + 1

steps.name: Block mirror descent update
steps.math: x_{k+1}^{(i)} = \begin{cases} \operatorname{argmin}_{u \in X_i} \left\{ \langle G_i(x_k, \xi_k), u \rangle + \frac{1}{\gamma_k} V_i(x_k^{(i)}, u) \right\}, & i = i_k, \\ x_k^{(i)}, & i \ne i_k \end{cases}

output.math: \text{After completing } k=1,\ldots,N, \text{ form the output blockwise from the incremental average state: } \bar{x}_N^{(i)} = \left( \sum_{k=1}^{N} \theta_k \right)^{-1} \left[s_{N+1}^{(i)} + x_{N+1}^{(i)} \sum_{j=u_i}^{N} \theta_j\right], \quad i=1,\ldots,b. \text{ Equivalently, } \bar{x}_N = \left( \sum_{k=1}^{N} \theta_k \right)^{-1} \sum_{k=1}^{N} (\theta_k x_k)

parameters.name: G_i(x_k, \xi_k)
parameters.math: G_i(x_k, \xi_k) \equiv U_i^T G(x_k, \xi_k) \text{ (i-th block of the stochastic subgradient)}

parameters.name: V(z, x)
parameters.math: V(z, x) = \sum_{i=1}^{b} p_i^{-1} V_i(z^{(i)}, x^{(i)}) \text{ (weighted aggregate Bregman divergence)}

proof.description: Apply Lemma 4.3 to the sampled block prox update (4.6.14), then lift the one-block descent bound to the aggregate potential V(z, x) = sum p_i^{-1} V_i(z, x)
proof.math: V(x_{k+1}, x) \le V(x_k, x) + \gamma_k \langle g(x_k), x - x_k \rangle + \gamma_k \delta_k + \frac{1}{2} \gamma_k^2 \bar{\delta}_k

proof.description: Use convexity of f to bound gamma_k [f(x_k) - f(x)] by gamma_k <g(x_k), x_k - x>, substitute the aggregate recursion (4.6.18), and telescope V(x_k, x) - V(x_{k+1}, x) over k = 1 to N
Take conditional expectation: E[delta_k | zeta_{[k-1]}] = 0 by independence of i_k and xi_k combined with the unbiased oracle condition (4.6.3)
Bound the quadratic stochastic term E[delta_bar_k] by expanding over the block sampling distribution and applying the block second-moment bound (4.6.4)
Take full expectation of the summed inequality (4.6.20), replace x by x_*, use E[delta_k] = 0 and E[delta_bar_k] <= sum M_i^2

key_lemmas.name: Lemma 4.3
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let } \zeta_1, \ldots, \zeta_j \text{ be a sequence of elements of } \mathbb{R}^n. \text{ Define } v_1 \in X^o \text{ and } v_{t+1} = \operatorname{argmin}_{x \in X} \{ \langle \zeta_t, x \rangle + V(v_t, x) \}. \text{ Then } \forall x \in X: \; \langle \zeta_t, v_t - x \rangle \le V(v_t, x) - V(v_{t+1}, x) + \frac{1}{2} \|\zeta_t\|_*^2, \quad \sum_{t=1}^{j} \langle \zeta_t, v_t - x \rangle \le V(v_1, x) + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{t=1}^{j} \|\zeta_t\|_*^2
key_lemmas.role: Provides the single-step Bregman descent estimate for a prox update that is applied to each sampled block

proof.description: Apply the three-point lemma (Lemma 3.4) to the prox update defining v_{t+1}
proof.math: \langle \zeta_t, v_{t+1} - x \rangle + V(v_t, v_{t+1}) \le V(v_t, x) - V(v_{t+1}, x)

proof.description: Bound <zeta_t, v_t - v_{t+1}> - V(v_t, v_{t+1}) using Cauchy-Schwarz and strong convexity V(v_t, v_{t+1}) >= (1/2)||v_t - v_{t+1}||^2
Combine steps 1 and 2 to get the per-step bound (4.1.41), then sum over t = 1 to j and telescope the V-terms to get (4.1.42)
proof.math: \langle \zeta_t, v_t - x \rangle \le V(v_t, x) - V(v_{t+1}, x) + \frac{1}{2} \|\zeta_t\|_*^2
